tests: framerail/tests/wikidot-legacy-actions.test.js#Rate sidecars bind only the exact renderer-owned control sequence
cases.result: Only recognized Rate modules whose compiled Wikidot controls match the renderer count receive typed plus, minus, and cancel descriptors. Authored lookalikes and cardinality drift leave all controls inert.
A star widget receives exactly the five server registry values 1 through 5. Plus and plus-minus registries cannot select a value outside their configured rating type.

tests: framerail/tests/wikidot-legacy-actions.test.js#Rate DOM is intercepted but remains inert without a typed sidecar
cases.result: Anonymous views receive no executable Rate sidecar. Private or route-mismatched targets fail at the existing permission boundary without exposing vote state.

tests: framerail/tests/page-vote-request-context.test.js#legacy Rate actions submit only a revision-bound server registry selector
framerail/tests/wikidot-legacy-action-request.test.js#Rate requests submit only the server registry binding
cases.result: The mutation reloads the current revision source and resolves the submitted index and fingerprint. Site, route page, and actor come from trusted request context; score, count, vote value, actor, and site are never accepted from the browser.
First vote, same-value replay, value change, cancel, and repeated cancel use one route-bound mutation and return the authoritative aggregate score.

The public page-view and mutation fixtures cover disabled rating, non-member and member policy, active locks, deleted pages, unviewable pages, route mismatch, and rating-type value mismatch. Cargo execution remains central work.

Vote mutations take an exclusive page row lock and the migration retains one newest current row before adding a partial unique index on page, actor, and rating system. A real two-transaction contention test remains central work.

The mutation returns ScoreService output from the same transaction, invalidates the site public-content fence after commit, and queues the exact page for rerender only when vote state changes. Candidate cache and navigation replay remains central work.

tests: framerail/tests/wikidot-legacy-actions.test.js#an action stays busy until its observable operation settles
framerail/tests/wikidot-legacy-action-request.test.js#server action failures remain observable to the action state machine
cases.result: Capture-phase handling preserves exact legacy onclick DOM, prevents authored JavaScript execution, suppresses repeated activation while pending, supports Space activation, and exposes server failure through the existing error surface.

No frozen live capture proves anonymous, non-member, member, moderator, and administrator control state or the exact existing-vote DOM across plus, plus-minus, and stars. The implementation does not invent those DOM differences.
The live star capture proves five selectable stars but does not prove a star-mode cancel control or gesture. No cancel UI is invented for star mode.

Production-mode focus restoration, mouse double click, loading/error intermediate paint, back/forward, navigation after rerender, CSRF rejection, and cache-fence timing require the exact candidate browser runtime.

the exact candidate covers every observable loading, success, error, focus, keyboard, double-submit, navigation, and cache interval without executing authored JavaScript
